chunks.title: Normal
chunks.text:
## Normal

No significant anomaly evidence.

Action:
- Continue routine monitoring.

chunks.title: Low
chunks.text:
## Low

Limited anomaly evidence affecting one sensor.

Action:
- Continue monitoring.
- Investigate if the condition persists.

chunks.title: Medium
chunks.text:
## Medium

Multiple sensor signals or moderate anomaly evidence.

Action:
- Increase monitoring.
- Request additional diagnostic evidence.

chunks.title: High
chunks.text:
## High

Strong anomaly evidence or significant sensor abnormalities.

Action:
- Escalate for operational assessment.
- Request additional diagnostic evidence.
- Notify maintenance personnel when appropriate.

chunks.title: Critical
chunks.text:
## Critical

Very strong anomaly evidence or multiple severe indicators.

Action:
- Immediately escalate for operational assessment.
- Request additional diagnostic evidence.
- Prioritize maintenance intervention.
- Do not automatically perform physical shutdown without authorized operational confirmation.

chunks.title: Pressure Inspection Procedure
chunks.text:
# Pressure Inspection Procedure

When abnormal pressure behavior is detected:

1. Verify the sensor reading.
2. Check upstream and downstream pressure conditions.
3. Inspect valves and connected piping.
4. Check for leakage or blockage.
5. Compare current pressure with normal operating conditions.
6. Escalate persistent abnormalities for maintenance assessment.

chunks.title: Mechanical Vibration
chunks.text:
## Mechanical Vibration

Abnormal vibration in rotating equipment can indicate mechanical problems.

Possible causes include:
- Bearing degradation
- Shaft misalignment
- Rotor imbalance
- Loose mounting
- Coupling problems

Recommended inspection:
1. Inspect bearings and rotating components.
2. Check shaft and coupling alignment.
3. Inspect equipment mounting.
4. Check for unusual mechanical noise.
5. Compare vibration with normal operating conditions.

chunks.title: Pressure Anomalies
chunks.text:
## Pressure Anomalies

Unexpected pressure changes may indicate:
- Leakage
- Blockage
- Valve problems
- Pump performance degradation

Recommended inspection:
1. Check pressure readings.
2. Inspect connected pipes and valves.
3. Check for visible leakage.
4. Verify pump operating conditions.

chunks.title: Vibration Inspection Procedure
chunks.text:
# Vibration Inspection Procedure

When abnormal vibration is detected:

1. Confirm that the vibration signal persists.
2. Inspect the pump and rotating equipment.
3. Check mounting bolts and structural supports.
4. Check shaft and coupling alignment.
5. Inspect bearings for visible damage or unusual conditions.
6. Record inspection observations.
7. Escalate persistent or severe abnormalities to maintenance personnel.

Do not assume a specific component has failed without supporting evidence.
